function: p. 1, 5-7: BeamNet predicts 1-bit RIS phase shifts from CSI and AllocationNet outputs RB allocation; BS beamforming is MRT with water-filling; jointly maximizes downlink sum rate.
system: p. 2, 7: BS with Nt=4 antennas, K=3 single-antenna users, passive reflecting RIS with M=64 1-bit elements, MISO-OFDMA, N=16 subcarriers of 180 kHz; carrier frequency not stated.
method: p. 5-7: Two convolutional networks (BeamNet, AllocationNet with SE-Res blocks), unsupervised training on sum-rate loss with QoS penalty, quantization layer and Gumbel softmax; five-stage phased training.
data_channel: p. 7-8: Custom simulated channels: Rayleigh direct link, Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user links, delay taps L0=4, L1=2, L2=3; 4,900 training and 100 validation samples.
test_conditions: p. 11-12: Trained with taps (4,2,3), R=10 m, Rician k=2/4 dB; tested with taps (6,3,4), R=15 m and other Rician factors; retraining needed for other N or M.
baselines: p. 8: Continuous and discrete SCA [35], random RB allocation, random RIS phases, no RIS, and the proposed network without quantization; no earlier learned method.
metrics: p. 8-12: System sum rate, 5th-percentile user rate versus QoS, runtime, and percentage of discrete-SCA performance.
complexity: p. 12: O(K^2 Nt N M + QM) for BeamNet, O(Q^2 Nt N K + QNK) for AllocationNet; runtime 17.58-20.49 ms versus 20,358-118,533 ms for discrete SCA (Table III).
q1_support: p. 7: "Rayleigh fading channels are assumed, while Rician fading is considered for the reflection channels". Custom simulator with path-loss exponents; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "the delay tap numbers in the testing environment are set to L0 = 6, L1 = 3, and L2 = 4, while the network is trained using datasets with delay tap numbers L0 = 4, L1 = 2, and L2 = 3". Also tested at R=15 m after training at R=10 m (Fig. 12) and over Rician factors after training at 2/4 dB (Fig. 13), without retraining.
q3_support: p. 8: "We compare the following methods in the simulation": continuous and discrete SCA [35] (non-learned), random allocation, random RIS, without RIS, and the proposed network without quantization. No earlier learned method is compared; the "entire training" variant (p. 10) is the proposed network trained another way.
q4_support: p. 12: "The computational complexity of BeamNet is given by O(K 2 Nt N M + QM )", and "Table III reports the runtime and performance of each algorithm" (17.58-20.49 ms for the proposed discrete algorithm).
q5_support: p. 8: "4,900 and 100 data samples were generated as the training and validation sets". Data come from the authors' own simulator; no code or data link and no public dataset appear in the 13 pages.
notes: Learned RB allocation (MAC-level) is trained jointly with the RIS phase shifts, a physical-layer decision, so the above_phy check passes. Area 3 because BeamNet outputs the RIS phase shifts; the BS beamformer (MRT and water-filling, p. 4) is not learned. The only comparisons with a learned model are the continuous variant (p. 8) and entire versus phased training (Fig. 8, p. 10), both variants of the proposed method, so q3 is 0. The PDF is the arXiv preprint (arXiv:2506.22448v1).
